newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican state reported quiet after attack.
newsitem.headline: Mexican state reported quiet after attack.

text.p: Mexico's southwestern state of Guerrero was reported quiet on Sunday, one day after four people were killed and several injured in a clash between police and guerrillas.
Radio reports said that police and military were searching for members of the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR) who attacked troops near the town of Tepozonalco around mid-day on Saturday.
Two army sergeants and two guerrillas carrying AK-47 assault rifles died in the clash, which took place about 60 miles (100 km) east of the state capital Chilpancingo.
Three army doctors were also injured in the incident, which a government statement said came as the army patrol returned from helping victims of a heavy hailstorm in the region.
But passengers on a bus who witnessed the clash said troops had carried out a surprise attack on EPR rebels who were handing out propaganda leaflets to drivers on the road.
The clash was the first reported this year between the military and the EPR, which sprang up in late June 1996 calling for a Marxist popular uprising to overthrow the federal government.

After a series of attacks at the end of August and subsequent sporadic shootings, the group lapsed into relative inactivity this year, saying it would instead concentrate on "armed propaganda." But it warned recently that it could restart its violent activities.
